headline: Argentina country risk rises 5.5% to near 800 points as dollar bonds drop
summary: Argentina's country risk index rose 5.5% to around 800 points, its highest level since October 2025, as US dollar-denominated bonds fell 1% on average and Wall Street equities declined.
why: Emerging market sovereign risk spreads measure debt default perceptions and influence domestic borrowing costs and capital flows.

entities.name: JP Morgan Emerging Markets Bond Index

impacts.name: Argentina
impacts.why: Spike in country risk signals diminished investor confidence in sovereign debt repayment capacity.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A jump in sovereign risk spreads and falling dollar-denominated bonds reflect broad capital flight and contagion from falling Wall Street indices.
